title: The Wheels We Keep Reinventing
content_html:

July 31 2026

The industry has a maddening relationship with solved problems. A thing gets figured out, packaged, documented, and shipped, and a decade later half the field is building it again from scratch. The old solution was rarely wrong. Somewhere along the way the proven thing got traded for something that looked cheaper, and it turned out more expensive the moment anyone counted the hours. I watch this happen on repeat and it wears on me.

Heroku did rolling deploys, blue/green releases, and health-checked rollbacks over a decade ago. You pushed to a remote and it handled the rest. Now every team running Kubernetes rebuilds that same machinery: readiness probes, deployment strategies, surge and unavailability tuning, rollback logic, and the observability to know when any of it went wrong. Kubernetes promised to hand you this. What it actually hands you is the primitives and a config surface large enough to get every piece of it subtly wrong. You traded a convenience you already had for a customization you now babysit every quarter, and somehow that counts as progress.

The Usual Suspects

Auth is the clearest case, and the one that irritates me most. There is no shortage of auth providers. Engineers write the same ad hoc routes anyway, the same users and sessions tables, the same password reset flow, the same JSON payloads, the same token refresh logic. Everyone knows the provider exists. They build it themselves regardless, ship it with at least one hole in it, and then maintain that hole forever.

Background jobs are the same story. You need to run arbitrary work outside the request cycle, so you wire together a queue, a worker pool, retry handling, dead letter behavior, and a way to see what failed. Sidekiq, Celery, and a dozen managed queues have existed for years. It gets rebuilt regardless, per stack, per team, per service.

Once you start looking, the list is long. A few others:

Retries, timeouts, backoff, and circuit breaking. Service meshes were supposed to own this so your application code never had to. Most retry logic still lives in the app, hand-written, usually without jitter and often applied to operations that were never safe to run twice.

Rate limiting. Token bucket and leaky bucket are old, well-described algorithms. Gateways offer rate limiting as a checkbox. It still gets reimplemented as middleware, often with a race condition around the counter.

Idempotency keys. Stripe wrote down the canonical pattern years ago and it is not complicated. Teams rebuild it per endpoint anyway, and get the retry-safety edge cases wrong in the process.

Feature flags. A managed service exists. Teams build a flags table and an admin page instead, then discover they have reinvented targeting rules and gradual rollout.

Caching and invalidation. Redis already exists. What gets hand-rolled is the part that was always hard: when to consider a cached value stale, and how to avoid serving the wrong thing.

Config and secrets. Parameter stores, Vault, Consul, and etcd all solve this. Every service still hand-writes its own loading, precedence, and validation, usually discovering the precedence bug in production.

Search. Postgres full text search and Elasticsearch both exist. The common path is a LIKE query, then a slow reinvention of relevance ranking once LIKE stops being enough.

State machines and workflows. Temporal and Step Functions exist to model long-running stateful work. The default is a status enum column and a growing pile of conditionals that no one can reason about after six months.

Multi-tenancy isolation. The tenant_id filter on every query is a wheel that has been built thousands of times, and the version with the security hole has been built almost as many.

The Pattern

The pattern underneath all of these is the same, and it is not subtle. A mature solution exists. The ecosystem swears a platform or provider already covers it. The engineer rebuilds it anyway, because the abstraction leaked, or did not fit the exact shape of the problem, or solved an adjacent problem and left a gap sitting right where the real work was. So you get half a solution you did not want and a second half you had to write yourself, which is the worst of both.

Keeping It Simple and Extensible

None of this is an argument for overengineering the first version. Keep it simple is still the right default, and I tell people that constantly. The point is narrower: do not engineer yourself into a box while you keep it simple. A small system and a system with every future decision already foreclosed can look identical on the first day.

Building the core product on standards and known protocols is what keeps the door open. If your auth speaks OIDC, swapping in a provider later is a configuration change. If your messaging speaks a documented protocol, adding an external system or a plugin is an integration rather than a rewrite. The trap is the opposite: hardcoded vendor dependencies, bespoke config formats, homegrown encodings, and undocumented patterns that no one wrote a test for. That version feels simple on day one and turns out to be the box, because everything you might want to add later has to be pried in against the grain.

Own It Without Rebuilding It

There is a real reason people avoid the managed version. A managed service is an external dependency that can fail on someone else's schedule, and it takes ownership of a piece of your system out of your hands. Most teams want agency over the things they run. That instinct is correct. When your auth provider has an outage, the outage is yours to explain and not yours to fix, and that is a genuinely bad position to be in.

The mistake is treating that instinct as a mandate to build from scratch. Those are not the only two options. The middle ground is a subsystem you can run locally and own end to end, without writing so much glue that you have effectively rebuilt it. Keycloak runs on your infrastructure and speaks standard protocols. Postgres, Redis, and NATS run locally and cover a large share of what the queue, cache, and messaging services were selling. You keep ownership without inheriting the maintenance burden of a bespoke implementation.

Running it yourself gets cheaper still when someone has written down how. Much of this boilerplate gets rebuilt because there is no agreed-upon document to follow, so every engineer rediscovers the same shape from first principles. An IETF-style specification, or even a well-scoped guideline, for how to build full text search or rate limiting that covers the ninety percent of use cases most systems actually have would turn a multi-week rediscovery into an afternoon of implementation. You would still write the code, but you would not be re-deriving the design every time. Stripe's idempotency-key writeup is proof it works: written down once, and anyone who reads it can build a correct version instead of a subtly broken one.

Watch the Level of Effort

The number worth watching is the ratio. Auth, queues, rate limiting, and deploys are par for the course. They are expected of any serious system and they are not the product. The effort spent on them should not exceed the effort spent on the thing that actually makes the product yours. When you find yourself several weeks deep in a hand-rolled job runner, the useful question is not whether it works but why that work is outcompeting the core product for your attention.

This is measurable, and most teams already measure it, which is the part that gets me. If your organization runs on sprint points and t-shirt sizes, the data is sitting right there. Pull the estimates and add up how much went to auth, deploy pipelines, queue plumbing, and rate limiting against the features only your product can offer. If the reinvented infrastructure is winning that comparison, your own estimates are telling you the team spent the quarter rebuilding things that already existed, and nobody read the number.

Sometimes the rebuild is justified. The proven thing genuinely does not fit, or the operational cost of adopting it exceeds the cost of a small custom version. That case is real and worth defending. The trouble is that most reinvention is not that case. It is a default reached for without checking whether the wheel already turns, and the bill comes later in maintenance, in the bug that the proven version had already fixed, and in the years of one engineer's time spent re-solving a problem that was solved before they started.

Before building the next piece of infrastructure, stop and check whether it is actually unsolved or only feels unsolved because the answer lives somewhere you did not bother to look. Most of the time it is solved. Run the proven version yourself and get back to the part of the job that is actually yours.

So you get half a solution you did not want and a second half you had to write yourself, which is the worst of both.

sentences.en: The pattern underneath all of these is the same, and it is not subtle.
sentences.zh: 所有这些背后的模式都是相同的，而且并不微妙。

sentences.en: A mature solution exists.
sentences.zh: 已有成熟的解决方案。

sentences.en: The ecosystem swears a platform or provider already covers it.
sentences.zh: 生态系统发誓平台或提供商已经涵盖了它。

sentences.en: The engineer rebuilds it anyway, because the abstraction leaked, or did not fit the exact shape of the problem, or solved an adjacent problem and left a gap sitting right where the real work was.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，工程师都会重建它，因为抽象泄漏了，或者不符合问题的确切形状，或者解决了相邻的问题并在实际工作所在的位置留下了空白。

sentences.en: So you get half a solution you did not want and a second half you had to write yourself, which is the worst of both.
sentences.zh: 所以你得到了一半你不想要的解决方案，而后半部分你必须自己编写，这是两者中最糟糕的。

blocks.html_en: Keeping It Simple and Extensible

sentences.en: Keeping It Simple and Extensible
sentences.zh: 保持简单和可扩展

blocks.html_en: None of this is an argument for overengineering the first version. Keep it simple is still the right default, and I tell people that constantly. The point is narrower: do not engineer yourself into a box while you keep it simple. A small system and a system with every future decision already foreclosed can look identical on the first day.

sentences.en: None of this is an argument for overengineering the first version.
sentences.zh: 这些都不是过度设计第一个版本的理由。

sentences.en: Keep it simple is still the right default, and I tell people that constantly.
sentences.zh: 保持简单仍然是正确的默认设置，我不断地告诉人们这一点。

sentences.en: The point is narrower: do not engineer yourself into a box while you keep it simple.
sentences.zh: 重点是：在保持简单的同时，不要将自己设计成一个盒子。

sentences.en: A small system and a system with every future decision already foreclosed can look identical on the first day.
sentences.zh: 一个小系统和一个已经取消了所有未来决策的系统在第一天看起来可能是一样的。

blocks.html_en: Building the core product on standards and known protocols is what keeps the door open. If your auth speaks OIDC, swapping in a provider later is a configuration change. If your messaging speaks a documented protocol, adding an external system or a plugin is an integration rather than a rewrite. The trap is the opposite: hardcoded vendor dependencies, bespoke config formats, homegrown encodings, and undocumented patterns that no one wrote a test for. That version feels simple on day one and turns out to be the box, because everything you might want to add later has to be pried in against the grain.

sentences.en: Building the core product on standards and known protocols is what keeps the door open.
sentences.zh: 基于标准和已知协议构建核心产品是保持大门敞开的原因。

sentences.en: If your auth speaks OIDC, swapping in a provider later is a configuration change.
sentences.zh: 如果您的身份验证使用 OIDC，则稍后交换提供程序就是配置更改。

sentences.en: If your messaging speaks a documented protocol, adding an external system or a plugin is an integration rather than a rewrite.
sentences.zh: 如果您的消息传递使用记录的协议，那么添加外部系统或插件就是集成而不是重写。

sentences.en: The trap is the opposite: hardcoded vendor dependencies, bespoke config formats, homegrown encodings, and undocumented patterns that no one wrote a test for.
sentences.zh: 陷阱恰恰相反：硬编码的供应商依赖项、定制的配置格式、自行开发的编码以及没有人编写测试的未记录的模式。

sentences.en: That version feels simple on day one and turns out to be the box, because everything you might want to add later has to be pried in against the grain.
sentences.zh: 这个版本在第一天感觉很简单，结果却是盒子，因为你以后可能想要添加的所有内容都必须根据实际情况进行撬动。

blocks.html_en: Own It Without Rebuilding It

sentences.en: Own It Without Rebuilding It
sentences.zh: 拥有它而不重建它

blocks.html_en: There is a real reason people avoid the managed version. A managed service is an external dependency that can fail on someone else's schedule, and it takes ownership of a piece of your system out of your hands. Most teams want agency over the things they run. That instinct is correct. When your auth provider has an outage, the outage is yours to explain and not yours to fix, and that is a genuinely bad position to be in.

sentences.en: There is a real reason people avoid the managed version.
sentences.zh: 人们回避托管版本是有真正原因的。

sentences.en: A managed service is an external dependency that can fail on someone else's schedule, and it takes ownership of a piece of your system out of your hands.
sentences.zh: 托管服务是一种外部依赖项，可能会按照其他人的计划发生故障，并且它会夺走您对系统的一部分的所有权。

sentences.en: Most teams want agency over the things they run.
sentences.zh: 大多数团队都希望对他们所管理的事情有代理权。

sentences.en: That instinct is correct.
sentences.zh: 这种直觉是正确的。

sentences.en: When your auth provider has an outage, the outage is yours to explain and not yours to fix, and that is a genuinely bad position to be in.
sentences.zh: 当您的身份验证提供商发生中断时，该中断由您来解释，而不是由您来修复，这确实是一个糟糕的处境。

blocks.html_en: The mistake is treating that instinct as a mandate to build from scratch. Those are not the only two options. The middle ground is a subsystem you can run locally and own end to end, without writing so much glue that you have effectively rebuilt it. Keycloak runs on your infrastructure and speaks standard protocols. Postgres, Redis, and NATS run locally and cover a large share of what the queue, cache, and messaging services were selling. You keep ownership without inheriting the maintenance burden of a bespoke implementation.

sentences.en: The mistake is treating that instinct as a mandate to build from scratch.
sentences.zh: 错误在于将这种本能视为从头开始构建的命令。

sentences.en: Those are not the only two options.
sentences.zh: 这些并不是唯一的两个选择。

sentences.en: The middle ground is a subsystem you can run locally and own end to end, without writing so much glue that you have effectively rebuilt it.
sentences.zh: 中间立场是一个可以在本地运行并拥有端到端的子系统，而无需编写太多的胶水来有效地重建它。

sentences.en: Keycloak runs on your infrastructure and speaks standard protocols.
sentences.zh: Keycloak 在您的基础设施上运行并使用标准协议。

sentences.en: Postgres, Redis, and NATS run locally and cover a large share of what the queue, cache, and messaging services were selling.
sentences.zh: Postgres、Redis 和 NATS 在本地运行，涵盖了队列、缓存和消息传递服务销售的大部分内容。

sentences.en: You keep ownership without inheriting the maintenance burden of a bespoke implementation.
sentences.zh: 您可以保留所有权，而无需承担定制实施的维护负担。

blocks.html_en: Running it yourself gets cheaper still when someone has written down how. Much of this boilerplate gets rebuilt because there is no agreed-upon document to follow, so every engineer rediscovers the same shape from first principles. An IETF-style specification, or even a well-scoped guideline, for how to build full text search or rate limiting that covers the ninety percent of use cases most systems actually have would turn a multi-week rediscovery into an afternoon of implementation. You would still write the code, but you would not be re-deriving the design every time. Stripe's idempotency-key writeup is proof it works: written down once, and anyone who reads it can build a correct version instead of a subtly broken one.

sentences.en: Running it yourself gets cheaper still when someone has written down how.
sentences.zh: 当有人写下如何运行时，你自己运行它会变得更便宜。

sentences.en: Much of this boilerplate gets rebuilt because there is no agreed-upon document to follow, so every engineer rediscovers the same shape from first principles.
sentences.zh: 由于没有商定的文件可遵循，大部分样板文件都会被重建，因此每个工程师都会从第一原理中重新发现相同的形状。

sentences.en: An IETF-style specification, or even a well-scoped guideline, for how to build full text search or rate limiting that covers the ninety percent of use cases most systems actually have would turn a multi-week rediscovery into an afternoon of implementation.
sentences.zh: 一个 IETF 风格的规范，或者甚至是一个范围广泛的指南，用于如何构建涵盖大多数系统实际拥有的 90% 用例的全文搜索或速率限制，会将数周的重新发现变成一个下午的实施。

sentences.en: You would still write the code, but you would not be re-deriving the design every time.
sentences.zh: 您仍然会编写代码，但不会每次都重新推导设计。

sentences.en: Stripe's idempotency-key writeup is proof it works: written down once, and anyone who reads it can build a correct version instead of a subtly broken one.
sentences.zh: Stripe 的幂等性密钥记录证明了它的有效性：写下来一次，任何阅读它的人都可以构建一个正确的版本，而不是一个被巧妙破坏的版本。

blocks.html_en: Watch the Level of Effort

sentences.en: Watch the Level of Effort
sentences.zh: 观察努力程度

blocks.html_en: The number worth watching is the ratio. Auth, queues, rate limiting, and deploys are par for the course. They are expected of any serious system and they are not the product. The effort spent on them should not exceed the effort spent on the thing that actually makes the product yours. When you find yourself several weeks deep in a hand-rolled job runner, the useful question is not whether it works but why that work is outcompeting the core product for your attention.

sentences.en: The number worth watching is the ratio.
sentences.zh: 值得关注的数字是比率。

sentences.en: Auth, queues, rate limiting, and deploys are par for the course.
sentences.zh: 身份验证、队列、速率限制和部署是本课程的标准内容。

sentences.en: They are expected of any serious system and they are not the product.
sentences.zh: 任何严肃的系统都需要它们，但它们不是产品。

sentences.en: The effort spent on them should not exceed the effort spent on the thing that actually makes the product yours.
sentences.zh: 在它们上花费的精力不应超过在真正使产品成为您的东西上花费的精力。

sentences.en: When you find yourself several weeks deep in a hand-rolled job runner, the useful question is not whether it works but why that work is outcompeting the core product for your attention.
sentences.zh: 当你发现自己在一个手工作业运行程序中投入了几周的时间时，有用的问题不是它是否有效，而是为什么该工作比核心产品更能吸引你的注意力。

blocks.html_en: This is measurable, and most teams already measure it, which is the part that gets me. If your organization runs on sprint points and t-shirt sizes, the data is sitting right there. Pull the estimates and add up how much went to auth, deploy pipelines, queue plumbing, and rate limiting against the features only your product can offer. If the reinvented infrastructure is winning that comparison, your own estimates are telling you the team spent the quarter rebuilding things that already existed, and nobody read the number.

sentences.en: This is measurable, and most teams already measure it, which is the part that gets me.
sentences.zh: 这是可以衡量的，大多数团队已经衡量了它，这是让我感兴趣的部分。

sentences.en: If your organization runs on sprint points and t-shirt sizes, the data is sitting right there.
sentences.zh: 如果您的组织以冲刺点和 T 恤尺寸为基础，那么数据就在那里。

sentences.en: Pull the estimates and add up how much went to auth, deploy pipelines, queue plumbing, and rate limiting against the features only your product can offer.
sentences.zh: 进行估算并根据只有您的产品才能提供的功能将用于身份验证、部署管道、队列管道和速率限制的费用相加。

sentences.en: If the reinvented infrastructure is winning that comparison, your own estimates are telling you the team spent the quarter rebuilding things that already existed, and nobody read the number.
sentences.zh: 如果重新设计的基础设施赢得了比较，那么您自己的估计告诉您，团队花了这个季度重建已经存在的东西，但没有人读到这个数字。

blocks.html_en: Sometimes the rebuild is justified. The proven thing genuinely does not fit, or the operational cost of adopting it exceeds the cost of a small custom version. That case is real and worth defending. The trouble is that most reinvention is not that case. It is a default reached for without checking whether the wheel already turns, and the bill comes later in maintenance, in the bug that the proven version had already fixed, and in the years of one engineer's time spent re-solving a problem that was solved before they started.

sentences.en: Sometimes the rebuild is justified.
sentences.zh: 有时重建是合理的。

sentences.en: The proven thing genuinely does not fit, or the operational cost of adopting it exceeds the cost of a small custom version.
sentences.zh: 经过验证的东西确实不适合，或者采用它的运营成本超过了小型定制版本的成本。

sentences.en: That case is real and worth defending.
sentences.zh: 这个案例是真实的，值得辩护。

sentences.en: The trouble is that most reinvention is not that case.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，大多数重塑并非如此。

sentences.en: It is a default reached for without checking whether the wheel already turns, and the bill comes later in maintenance, in the bug that the proven version had already fixed, and in the years of one engineer's time spent re-solving a problem that was solved before they started.
sentences.zh: 这是在不检查轮子是否已经转动的情况下达到的默认值，并且账单是在维护后期、在经过验证的版本已经修复的错误中以及在一位工程师花费数年时间重新解决在他们开始之前解决的问题中出现的。

blocks.html_en: Before building the next piece of infrastructure, stop and check whether it is actually unsolved or only feels unsolved because the answer lives somewhere you did not bother to look. Most of the time it is solved. Run the proven version yourself and get back to the part of the job that is actually yours.

sentences.en: Before building the next piece of infrastructure, stop and check whether it is actually unsolved or only feels unsolved because the answer lives somewhere you did not bother to look.
sentences.zh: 在构建下一个基础设施之前，停下来检查它是否实际上没有解决，或者只是感觉没有解决，因为答案就在你懒得去寻找的地方。

sentences.en: Most of the time it is solved.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候都可以解决。

sentences.en: Run the proven version yourself and get back to the part of the job that is actually yours.
sentences.zh: 自己运行经过验证的版本，然后回到实际属于您的工作部分。

content_html_zh:
[主要] [随笔] [文章] [项目] [现在] [简历] [讲座]

July 31 2026

该行业与已解决的问题有着令人抓狂的关系。 一个东西被弄清楚、打包、记录和运输，十年后，一半的领域正在从头开始重新构建它。 旧的解决方案很少出错。 一路走来，经过验证的东西被换成了看起来更便宜的东西，而当人们计算时间时，结果发现它更贵。 我看着这样的事情不断发生，这让我感到厌烦。

Heroku 十多年前就进行了滚动部署、蓝/绿发布和健康检查回滚。 你按下遥控器，它就会处理剩下的事情。 现在，每个运行 Kubernetes 的团队都会重建相同的机制：就绪探针、部署策略、激增和不可用性调整、回滚逻辑以及了解何时出错的可观察性。 Kubernetes 答应给你这个。 它实际上提供给你的是原语和一个足够大的配置表面，足以让它的每一部分都出现微妙的错误。 你用已有的便利换取了现在每个季度都会进行的定制，这在某种程度上算作进步。

通常的嫌疑人

Auth 是最明显的情况，也是最让我恼火的情况。 不乏身份验证提供商。 无论如何，工程师都会编写相同的临时路由、相同的用户和会话表、相同的密码重置流程、相同的 JSON 有效负载、相同的令牌刷新逻辑。 每个人都知道提供商的存在。 不管怎样，他们自己建造它，运送时至少有一个洞，然后永远维护这个洞。

后台工作也是同样的情况。 您需要在请求周期之外运行任意工作，因此您将队列、工作池、重试处理、死信行为以及查看失败的方法连接在一起。 Sidekiq、Celery 和十几个托管队列已经存在多年了。 无论每个堆栈、每个团队、每个服务，它都会被重建。

一旦你开始寻找，清单就会很长。 其他一些：

重试、超时、退避和熔断。 服务网格应该拥有它，因此您的应用程序代码永远不必拥有它。 大多数重试逻辑仍然存在于应用程序中，是手写的，通常没有抖动，并且通常应用于永远无法安全运行两次的操作。

速率限制。 令牌桶和漏桶是古老的、描述良好的算法。 网关提供速率限制作为复选框。 它仍然被重新实现为中间件，通常会出现竞争条件。

幂等键。 Stripe 几年前就写下了规范模式，并不复杂。 无论如何，团队都会根据端点重建它，并在此过程中出现重试安全边缘情况错误。

功能标志。 存在托管服务。 相反，团队构建了一个标志表和一个管理页面，然后发现他们重新发明了定位规则并逐步推出。

缓存和失效。 Redis 已经存在。 手工处理的部分始终是困难的：何时考虑缓存值过时，以及如何避免提供错误的服务。

配置和秘密。 参数存储、Vault、Consul 和 etcd 都解决了这个问题。 每个服务仍然手工编写自己的加载、优先级和验证，通常会在生产中发现优先级错误。

搜索。 Postgres 全文搜索和 Elasticsearch 都存在。 常见的路径是 LIKE 查询，然后一旦 LIKE 不再足够，就会缓慢地重新发明相关性排名。

状态机和工作流程。 时间函数和步骤函数的存在是为了对长期运行的有状态工作进行建模。 默认值是一个状态枚举列和一堆不断增加的条件，六个月后无人能推理出这些条件。

多租户隔离。 每个查询上的tenant_id过滤器都是一个已经构建了数千次的轮子，并且存在安全漏洞的版本几乎已经构建了同样多的次数。

模式

所有这些背后的模式都是相同的，而且并不微妙。 已有成熟的解决方案。 生态系统发誓平台或提供商已经涵盖了它。 无论如何，工程师都会重建它，因为抽象泄漏了，或者不符合问题的确切形状，或者解决了相邻的问题并在实际工作所在的位置留下了空白。 所以你得到了一半你不想要的解决方案，而后半部分你必须自己编写，这是两者中最糟糕的。

保持简单和可扩展

这些都不是过度设计第一个版本的理由。 保持简单仍然是正确的默认设置，我不断地告诉人们这一点。 重点是：在保持简单的同时，不要将自己设计成一个盒子。 一个小系统和一个已经取消了所有未来决策的系统在第一天看起来可能是一样的。

基于标准和已知协议构建核心产品是保持大门敞开的原因。 如果您的身份验证使用 OIDC，则稍后交换提供程序就是配置更改。 如果您的消息传递使用记录的协议，那么添加外部系统或插件就是集成而不是重写。 陷阱恰恰相反：硬编码的供应商依赖项、定制的配置格式、自行开发的编码以及没有人编写测试的未记录的模式。 这个版本在第一天感觉很简单，结果却是盒子，因为你以后可能想要添加的所有内容都必须根据实际情况进行撬动。

拥有它而不重建它

人们回避托管版本是有真正原因的。 托管服务是一种外部依赖项，可能会按照其他人的计划发生故障，并且它会夺走您对系统的一部分的所有权。 大多数团队都希望对他们所管理的事情有代理权。 这种直觉是正确的。 当您的身份验证提供商发生中断时，该中断由您来解释，而不是由您来修复，这确实是一个糟糕的处境。

错误在于将这种本能视为从头开始构建的命令。 这些并不是唯一的两个选择。 中间立场是一个可以在本地运行并拥有端到端的子系统，而无需编写太多的胶水来有效地重建它。 Keycloak 在您的基础设施上运行并使用标准协议。 Postgres、Redis 和 NATS 在本地运行，涵盖了队列、缓存和消息传递服务销售的大部分内容。 您可以保留所有权，而无需承担定制实施的维护负担。

当有人写下如何运行时，你自己运行它会变得更便宜。 由于没有商定的文件可遵循，大部分样板文件都会被重建，因此每个工程师都会从第一原理中重新发现相同的形状。 一个 IETF 风格的规范，或者甚至是一个范围广泛的指南，用于如何构建涵盖大多数系统实际拥有的 90% 用例的全文搜索或速率限制，会将数周的重新发现变成一个下午的实施。 您仍然会编写代码，但不会每次都重新推导设计。 Stripe 的幂等性密钥记录证明了它的有效性：写下来一次，任何阅读它的人都可以构建一个正确的版本，而不是一个被巧妙破坏的版本。

观察努力程度

值得关注的数字是比率。 身份验证、队列、速率限制和部署是本课程的标准内容。 任何严肃的系统都需要它们，但它们不是产品。 在它们上花费的精力不应超过在真正使产品成为您的东西上花费的精力。 当你发现自己在一个手工作业运行程序中投入了几周的时间时，有用的问题不是它是否有效，而是为什么该工作比核心产品更能吸引你的注意力。
